request.query: The coefficient l1 norm of a monomial equals the norm of its coefficient

items.informal_description: The Gauss norm of the monomial polynomial $ rX^n $ is equal to $ v(r) \cdot c^n $, where $ v $ is a valuation on the semiring $ R $ and $ c $ is a real number parameter.

  [inst_2 : NormedAlgebra 𝕜 E] (c : ℕ → 𝕜) (n : ℕ) [NormOneClass E], ‖FormalMultilinearSeries.ofScalars E c n‖ = ‖c n‖
items.informal_description: For a formal multilinear series constructed from scalar coefficients $ c : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{K} $ in a normed field $ \mathbb{K} $ with $ \|1\| = 1 $, the norm of the $ n $-th term is equal to the norm of the scalar $ c(n) $, i.e., $ \|\text{ofScalars}_n(c)\| = \|c(n)\| $.

items.informal_name: Gauss Norm of Monomial: $ \|rX^n\|_{v,c} = v(r) c^n $
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u_1} {F : Type u_2} [inst : Semiring R] [inst_1 : FunLike F R ℝ] (v : F) {c : ℝ} (r : R)
  [ZeroHomClass F R ℝ] [NonnegHomClass F R ℝ],
  0 ≤ c → ∀ (n : ℕ), PowerSeries.gaussNorm v c ((PowerSeries.monomial n) r) = v r * c ^ n
items.informal_description: For a monomial $ rX^n $ in the ring of power series over a semiring $ R $, the Gauss norm $ \|rX^n\|_{v,c} $ with respect to a valuation $ v $ and a non-negative real number $ c $ is equal to $ v(r) \cdot c^n $. This holds for any $ r \in R $, natural number $ n $, and non-negative $ c $. The Gauss norm is defined as the supremum of $ v(f_i) \cdot c^i $ over all coefficients $ f_i $ of the power series.

items.informal_name: Mahler Measure of Constant Polynomial Equals Modulus
items.informal_description: For any complex number $ z $, the Mahler measure of the constant polynomial $ z $ is equal to the modulus of $ z $, i.e., $ \text{MahlerMeasure}(z) = |z| $.

items.informal_description: For any extended non-negative real number $ p $ with $ 0 < p $, index $ i $, and element $ x $ in the normed additive commutative group $ E_i $, the norm of the function in the $ L^p $ space that takes the value $ x $ at index $ i $ and zero elsewhere is equal to the norm of $ x $.
